newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Bangkok Bank, Sinar Mas launch.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Bangkok Bank, Sinar Mas launch.

text.p: Asian debt markets offered a couple of new deals on Tuesday following a long holiday weekend in Hong Kong.
HSBC Markets launched for Bangkok Bank a US$150 million floating rate certificate of deposit issue.
The certificates have a final maturity of seven years but can be put after five. They pay a margin of 18.75 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate.
With fees, the all-in return to co-lead managers committing to US$5-7 million is 24 basis points, while senior managers committing to US$3-4 million receive 23 basis points.
Bangkok Bank has a couple of outstanding issues.
There is a note due in June 1998 with a coupon of six-month LIBOR plus 42.5 basis points that is currently trading at about 15 basis points over the benchmark.
Another deal due June 1999 has a coupon of LIBOR plus 40 and is trading at around 18 basis points over LIBOR.
Bangkok Bank is Thailand's largest bank. It is rated A2 by Moody's Investors Service and A-minus by Standard and Poor's Corp.
Sinar Mas Finance, a unit of Indonesian conglomerate Sinar Mas Multiartha, launched a US$50 million floating rate note issue via Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Singapore.
The notes have a final maturity of three years but can be put at the first or second anniversary.
The notes pay a margin of 137.5 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate. With fees, the all-in return to top-tier managers is 163 basis points.
Sinar Mas has tapped the capital markets a number of times via its subsidiaries, notably Bank International Indonesia, but this is the first FRN issued under the Sinar Mas name.
The deal is the first issue off the borrower's US$250 million Asian Currency Note Programme.
Proceeds of the issue will be used for general working capital.
Sinar Mas has been in the news lately with its white knight takeover of troubled Singapore company Amcol Holdings.
Sinar Mas last week said it would inject assets worth more than US$2.4 billion into a new company to be formed to take over Amcol.
Investors attending roadshows for the FRN were unruffled by the Sinar Mas purchase and response to the issue has been strong, a syndicate manager at DMG said.
Korea Development Bank on Monday launched a 30 billion yen Samurai bond via Nomura Securities. The bond is due in September 2001, carries a coupon of 2.45 percent and was priced at 99.90.

On Sunday, a Chinese newspaper quoted a Ministry of Finance official as saying that China will make frequent issues of sovereign debt over the next few years, focusing on markets in the U.S., Japan and Europe.
Looking at the rest of the week, a US$150 million FRCD for Indonesia's Bank Central Asia may be launched on Wednesday through LTCB Asia.
Taiwan's First Commercial Bank is expected to take its first international FRCD issue to the market later this week. Citicorp and WestLB are the arrangers.
Pidemco Land's US$120 million floating rate note issue may be "soft-launched" this week by Standard Chartered Investment Banking.
Union Bank of Hong Kong's FRCD may be launched on Friday through Bayerische Landesbank and Jardine Fleming.
KEB Hong Kong's HK$ FRCD looks set for launch by the middle of next week. Arrangers are Chase Asia, Jardine Fleming and Sakura Finance Asia.
